title: Why a passing siren drops in pitch
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why does an ambulance siren change pitch as it passes?
Does the ambulance driver hear the pitch change?

explain.say: An ambulance siren makes the same note all the time. Yet as it races past you, the sound you hear suddenly drops from high to low.

draw.text: Why a passing siren drops in pitch

explain.say: As the ambulance comes towards you, it chases its own sound waves. Each new wave starts a little closer to you, so the waves bunch up and arrive more often, and you hear a higher pitch.
As it passes, the change is sudden. Behind the moving ambulance, each wave starts a little farther away, so the waves are stretched out and arrive less often: a lower pitch.
This change of pitch caused by motion is called the Doppler effect. The ambulance crew hears a steady note, because they are moving with the siren.

faq.a: The Doppler effect is the change in pitch you hear when a sound source moves towards or away from you. Coming closer squashes the waves for a higher pitch; moving away stretches them for a lower pitch.

faq.q: Why does an ambulance siren change pitch as it passes?
faq.a: Approaching, its sound waves are squashed together and reach you more often, so the pitch is higher. Moving away, they are stretched apart, so the pitch drops as it goes past.
asks: Why does a car sound go neeeoww?
Why does a train horn change as it passes?

faq.q: Does the ambulance driver hear the pitch change?
faq.a: No. The driver moves along with the siren, so the waves reach them at a steady rate and the pitch stays the same.
asks: Does the siren sound the same inside the ambulance?

faq.q: How was the Doppler effect tested?
faq.a: Christian Doppler described it in 1842. In 1845 Christophorus Buys Ballot tested it with trumpeters playing on a moving train while musicians beside the track listened to the pitch change.
asks: What was the train and trumpet experiment?

faq.q: Is the Doppler effect used for anything?
faq.a: Yes. Doctors use it in ultrasound to measure blood flow, weather radar uses it with radio waves to measure wind in storms, and astronomers use it with light to measure how fast stars move.
asks: What are uses of the Doppler effect?

facts: Christian Doppler described the effect named after him in 1842.
In 1845 Buys Ballot confirmed the Doppler effect for sound using trumpeters on a moving train.

quiz.say: An ambulance races past you with its siren on. What does the paramedic inside hear?
quiz.show: Inside the ambulance, the siren sounds…

options.show: High, then low as it passes you
options.say: High, then low as it passes you

quiz.why: The paramedic moves with the siren, so the waves reach them at a steady rate and there is no Doppler change.

wrong.0: Only a listener the siren moves towards and then away from hears the drop.
wrong.2: The siren is still loud inside; only the pitch change is missing.
